questions.q: In a tiered steady-state support model, what does Tier 1 typically handle?
options: Genuine Oracle product defects
How-to questions and simple navigation issues, often via super users or an internal help desk
Formal Service Requests filed with Oracle
Enterprise structure redesign
questions.explain: Tier 1 is usually an internal help desk or super users handling how-to questions and simple navigation issues.

questions.q: When is it appropriate to open an Oracle Service Request (SR)?
options: Immediately, for any question of any kind
Only when the Executive Sponsor personally requests it
Only during hypercare, never afterward
Once Tier 1 and Tier 2 have ruled out configuration or user error and the issue looks like a genuine product defect
questions.explain: An SR is appropriate once internal tiers have ruled out configuration or user error, and the issue appears to require Oracle's direct intervention.

questions.q: What does Oracle's Severity 1 classification mean?
options: Production use is stopped or so severely impacted that work cannot reasonably continue
A minor inconvenience with an available workaround
A general question with no urgency
A cosmetic UI issue
questions.explain: Severity 1 means production is stopped or so severely impacted that the business cannot reasonably continue, triggering 24x7 response from Oracle.

questions.q: What risk comes from overstating or understating an SR's severity?
options: Overstating speeds up any fix; there is no downside
Severity has no effect on response time
Overstating doesn't actually speed up a non-critical fix, while understating a critical issue delays the response it needs
Severity can only be set by Oracle, never the customer
questions.explain: Matching the right severity matters: overstating doesn't speed up a non-urgent fix, and understating a truly critical issue delays the urgent response it needs.

questions.q: How was Brightfield's post-go-live rounding discrepancy in the Cash Management report resolved?
options: It was ignored since it was minor
Logged as a Severity 3 SR after Tier 2 couldn't trace it, with Oracle fixing it in the next quarterly update
Escalated immediately to Severity 1
Fixed by rebuilding the entire configuration workbook
questions.explain: After internal Tier 2 support couldn't trace the cause, it was logged as a Severity 3 SR (a minor loss with a workaround), and Oracle resolved it in a later quarterly update.
